transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Nebula Head of Cloud Partnerships), Sofia Alvarez (Nebula Strategic Alliances), Ethan Park (Nebula Solutions Architect)

Summary:
Quick co-sell pipeline sync to align on target accounts, discuss technical blockers for a few Tier 1 prospects, and agree on next steps for a joint pilot and benchmarks. Heavy focus on Dedicated vs Hosted economics and data residency / KMS requirements for three Fortune-type accounts.

Topics:
- Pipeline overview and top 6 accounts
- Technical readiness: benchmarks, VPC/private deployment questions
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM
- Commercial asks: pricing bands, co-sell motion, executive intro timing

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, uh thanks for carving out time, appreciated. Quick intro from our side, I'm Alex, I'll run the partnership side, Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Marcus: Thanks Alex, Marcus here, Sofia and Ethan on from my side. We got about 55 minutes, so maybe we walk the pipeline then dig into the technical asks.
[00:00:22] Priya: Sounds good, I'll jump in on infra and benchmarks.
[00:00:30] Alex: Cool. Marcus, do you want to start with the pipeline? Top accounts, timing, where you want Redwood to lean in.
[00:00:38] Marcus: Yeah. So we have six target accounts that are heads down for Q1, three of them are big regulated financials, one healthcare payer, one e-comm, one platform/marketplace. The three regs are the ones asking for on-prem or VPC-based private deployments and key management requirements. They're the highest ACV.
[00:01:02] Sofia: And just to add, decision timelines vary — one of the banks expects an RFP in Jan, the healthcare payer wants a pilot in Feb. The rest are a bit later.
[00:01:13] Alex: Great — that aligns with the co-sell window we talked about. For the regulated ones, we'd recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS; that gives the audit and data residency controls.
[00:01:24] Ethan: Quick question — when you say Private, is that the same as the VPC option you mentioned in the deck or is there an on-prem package? Which customers typically go on-prem vs VPC?
[00:01:36] Priya: Good Q. We offer both VPC-hosted private control plane and a fully on-prem package. On-prem is rarer, usually for air-gapped or super regulated environments. For the banks we've seen VPC with KMS integration and strict audit logs meet their needs 80% of the time.
[00:01:52] Marcus: For these banks, they specifically asked about HSM-backed keys and audit retention of seven years. Can Redwood support that?
[00:02:03] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS and can broker with HSM in the flow; audit retention typically configurable, we'll need to check retention SLA for seven years but it's something we've enabled for other enterprise customers.
[00:02:16] Alex: We'll capture that as an action — Priya to validate HSM and 7-year retention.
[00:02:21] [00:02:21] Sofia: On the commercial side, they'll want a predictability guarantee — they asked for Dedicated capacity with reserved throughput. How flexible is your Dedicated SKU around scaling and burst?
[00:02:34] Priya: Dedicated is designed for reserve pools, autoscaling policies, and burst options. You can configure a base committed capacity and an overflow burst which we'll bill at a higher rate. The other tradeoff is latency predictability vs unit cost.
[00:02:50] Marcus: We're hearing pushback from procurement about unit cost vs latency. If we pitch Dedicated, they want a clear TCO comparison versus hosted. Can you run a TCO with typical usage patterns?
[00:03:02] Alex: Yes — we can send a TCO model. We'll include the cost for hosted API, Dedicated with 3 size tiers, and a quick sensitivity table for tokens and concurrency. I'll include that in the commercial package.
[00:03:13] [00:03:13] Ethan: For the bank's PoC, they want a throughput of ~300 requests per second with avg token generation of 120 tokens and 99th latency under 350ms. Any existing reference points?
[00:03:26] Priya: That's a pretty heavy profile. 300 rps @ 120 tokens is doable with Dedicated and optimized batching and KV cache. 99th at 350ms depends on model size and quantization — if they accept a smaller open model variant or quantized weights we can hit it. We'll need to run a benchmark under their request distribution.
[00:03:44] Alex: Also routing policies help — route latency-sensitive traffic to a lower-capacity, higher-cost lane and non-critical to cheaper pools. We can present model variants and quant profiles that meet their latency SLA for conversational flows.
[00:03:58] [00:03:58] Marcus: There's sensitivity around PII and derivative data. They asked about prompt logging — can you redact or opt out of logging prompts on Private deployments?
[00:04:09] Priya: On Private, logs can be configured to avoid storing prompts, or to store hashed representations for debugging. On Hosted, we have GDPR-friendly retention controls but Private gives them full control. We'll want to document exactly what's logged so procurement is comfortable.
[00:04:23] Sofia: Good. For the executive ask — they want a short one-pager co-sell GTM and an exec intro so C-suite can see the value.
[00:04:32] Alex: We'll draft a joint one-pager and send a CEO/Head of Partnerships intro template.
[00:04:37] [00:04:37] Ethan: Switching to technical blockers — one prospect uses an internal inference service and is worried about model drift and model validation during rollouts. How does Redwood handle rollouts?
[00:04:49] Priya: We support canary and A/B rollouts, automatic fallback policies, and evaluation hooks tied to prompt sets. We also expose trace hooks for custom validators so you can run quality checks before full rollout.
[00:05:02] Marcus: Do you keep a history of model versions and retrain metadata? They want an audit trail for inference decisions.
[00:05:10] Priya: We version model artifacts and keep metadata for rollouts; audit logs can be exported to the customer's SIEM for long-term retention.
[00:05:17] [00:05:17] Marcus: Excellent. On procurement, one of the banks mandates SOC2 type 2, ISO 27001, and penetration test reports. Do you have those artifacts?
[00:05:28] Alex: Yes — we have SOC2 Type II and ISO certs in our security kit. We'll share the security pack and pen test summary; there might be NDA gating for some docs.
[00:05:37] Sofia: They also asked about SSO/SAML and RBAC tie-ins to Okta and Azure AD.
[00:05:42] Priya: We support SAML SSO and role-based access; integration with Okta/Azure AD is standard. We'll attach an integration checklist for them.
[00:05:50] [00:05:50] Marcus: Perfect. For the PoC success criteria — the bank wants three main metrics: latency (99th < 350ms), accuracy measured on our 200-case prompt set (precision > 92%), and cost per token below a target. Can Redwood ingest a custom eval set?
[00:06:05] Priya: Yes — we can run evaluations with a custom prompt set and produce regression alerts. We'll need the test harness and the scoring rubric.
[00:06:13] Alex: We'll include that as part of the pilot plan. Priya will coordinate the benchmark plan with Ethan.
[00:06:19] [00:06:19] Ethan: On infra, the bank requires that model weights cannot be exported off their VPC. Is that supported?
[00:06:26] Priya: With Private VPC we can restrict artifact export; model serving can happen entirely inside the customer's network. We need to capture exact contractual language for that.
[00:06:35] Alex: We'll draft contract clauses about data-in-place and model artifact residency.
[00:06:40] [00:06:40] Marcus: Let's talk competitive positioning. We're hearing Anthropic and OpenAI being evaluated. How do we position Redwood in those RFPs?
[00:06:49] Alex: Redwood is production-first — emphasize deterministic economics, Dedicated capacity options, and the observability/rollout tooling. If the customer prioritizes open weights or quantization, we can show our model catalog and verified performance profiles. Also highlight private deployment and KMS/HSM options which are not always standard in hosted APIs.
[00:07:05] Sofia: Procurement also asked about support SLAs and escalation paths.
[00:07:10] Alex: We offer SLA-backed Dedicated contracts with priority support and named CSMs on enterprise tiers. We'll include a sample support escalation matrix.
[00:07:17] [00:07:17] Ethan: For the pilot, they need a small test harness — is there a Redwood reference app or quickstart we can hand to their infra team?
[00:07:26] Priya: Yes, we have quickstarts, a reference app, and an evaluation harness. We'll share a GitHub link and a step-by-step for spinning up test infra. Eph — I mean Ethan, we'll include the infra checklist for VPC peering, subnets, security groups, and KMS setup.
[00:07:41] Marcus: Haha, no worries. Okay, the other ask is joint account planning — we want to run a co-sell motion and get Redwood sales to join a few exec calls. How do you normally structure the co-sell?
[00:07:52] Alex: Typically we do a joint one-pager per target account, assign an AE and partner rep, and run an aligned outreach playbook — joint meetings, shared pipeline tracker, and quarterly exec touchpoints. We'll provide a template.
[00:08:05] [00:08:05] Sofia: Do you have a co-sell compensation model or partner discount tiers we can show? They asked about margins.
[00:08:12] Alex: We have partner discount tiers based on committed volume and whether it's referral vs co-sell. I'll share the partner pricing bands; final terms are negotiated in the partner contract.
[00:08:21] Priya: Also on the tech side, one of the prospects is interested in model quantization to lower cost. We should align on which models we recommend and expected perf delta.
[00:08:30] Ethan: Are there benchmarks for quantized models vs float?
[00:08:33] Priya: Yes, we have internal perf profiles — quantized can reduce memory and increase throughput but there is an accuracy tradeoff. We'll include example profiles for the model family they prefer.
[00:08:44] [00:08:44] Marcus: Lastly, for the bank PoC timeline — can we aim to start baseline benchmarks the week of Jan 8th and a live pilot mid-February?
[00:08:54] Alex: That's reasonable. We'll aim to have the benchmark plan and infra checklist to you by 12/11 so you can spin up early Jan.
[00:09:02] Sofia: Sounds good.
[00:09:05] [00:09:05] Alex: Ok quick recap of owners: Alex send co-sell deck + pricing by 12/08; Priya send benchmark plan + infra checklist by 12/11 and schedule the technical deep dive with Ethan for week of 12/13; Marcus to share pipeline spreadsheet by 12/10. Anything else?
[00:09:21] Marcus: Could you also include sample contract language around data residency and model export restrictions?
[00:09:26] Alex: Yes will do.
[00:09:28] [00:09:28] Sofia: We'll put together the internal RFP timeline and send it to Alex so we can align resources.
[00:09:35] Alex: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the attachments.
[00:09:39] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:09:41] Marcus: Thanks.
[00:09:43] Sofia: Bye.

Notes / Imperfections:
